newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch PTT calls off talks with Philips.
newsitem.headline: Dutch PTT calls off talks with Philips.

text.p: Dutch post and telecoms group PTT Nederland NV said on Monday it had called off talks with Philips Communications on the combination of their cable TV interests.
"We started talks about a year and a half ago aiming at enlarging our market share in the cable market," a Dutch PTT spokeswoman said. "We could not come to a conclusion."
Philips and Dutch PTT said around a year ago they were in talks to create a European firm with 3.5 million cable connections.

"After a detailed study of possible options, the parties have come to the conclusion that there are insufficient grounds for strategic collaboration. KPN now will continue consultations with other parties about possible joint ventures," Dutch PTT said in a statement.

Philips has combined with United International Holdings in a joint venture called UPC resulting in the biggest privately held cable firm in Europe with over two million connections in around 10 countries.

Dutch PTT owns around 77 percent of Casema, a 26-year old cable company that reaches 1.2 million Dutch households. Casema has a pay-per-view joint venture with TeleSelect, a joint venture between Philips, Dutch PTT and Graff Pay per View of the U.S.
